question: The Hornbill Festival is celebrated in the state of ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**3) Nagaland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hornbill Festival is an annual cultural festival celebrated in the state of **Nagaland, India**.
 
• It is organized by the Government of Nagaland to promote the rich cultural heritage of the 16 major tribes and sub-tribes of the state.
 
• The festival is named after the **Hornbill bird**, which is considered a symbol of respect and folklore in Naga culture.
 
• It is celebrated **from December 1 to 10** every year at the Naga Heritage Village, Kisama, near Kohima, the capital of Nagaland.
 
• The festival includes cultural performances, traditional music, dance, food, crafts, and a variety of events like the Hornbill International Rock Contest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagaland:**

 
 
• Nagaland is located in the northeastern region of India and shares its borders with Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, and Manipur, as well as Myanmar.
 
• The state is known for its diverse tribes, each having its own unique traditions, language, and festivals.
 
 
 
• **Hornbill Bird:**
 
 
• The Hornbill bird is a large, colorful bird found in the tropical and subtropical regions of Asia and Africa.
 
• It holds a significant place in Naga folklore and symbolizes the rich biodiversity of the region.
 
 
 
• **Tourism Impact:**
 
 
• The Hornbill Festival attracts both domestic and international tourists, boosting the local economy and promoting cultural exchange.
 
• It is often referred to as the "Festival of Festivals" and serves as a platform for showcasing the state’s cultural vibrancy.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage:**
 
 
• Festivals like the Hornbill Festival contribute to the preservation of intangible cultural heritage, which is recognized as vital by UNESCO.
